facts.fact: The Deputy Minister of Home Affairs told the National Assembly on 15 May 2026 that the department intends in 2026/27 to automate the birth process at health facilities for first registrations of citizens, which he said would end the generation of paper records; it is stated as an intention, not as a system in use.
facts.system: automated birth process at health facilities

systems.system: automated birth process at health facilities
systems.owner: Department of Home Affairs, Civic Services Branch
systems.tiers: health facilities; planned for 2026/27, first registrations of citizens; 680,555 babies registered within 30 days of birth in 2025/26 against a target of 677,000
more than 60 million civic records digitised since inception; a further 25 million targeted for 2026/27
6,304 site visits in 2025/26, of which 5,010 public schools and 516 special schools; rural, remote and disaster-affected communities; identity documents and replacement birth certificates
just over four million issued in 2025/26
